SE1.text: A metric embedding φ: O → R^d with minimum inter-object distance a. That is: φ assigns positions in Euclidean space to CCA objects, and a = min_{m ∈ M} |φ(tgt(m)) − φ(src(m))| > 0 is the shortest step length.
SE1.what_it_introduces: A spatial scale: a ∈ ℝ_{>0} with units [m].

SE2.text: Isotropy: the spacing a is the same in all directions. That is: |φ(tgt(m)) − φ(src(m))| = a for every morphism m ∈ M.
free_parameters: a (still free — SE2 does not fix its numerical value)
SE2.what_it_introduces: A single uniform step length a (rather than a_x ≠ a_y ≠ a_z).

SE3.text: Uniform time: each morphism has temporal duration dt. That is: a clock assigns to every m ∈ M a duration dt ∈ ℝ_{>0} [s], and dt is the same for all m.
SE3.what_it_introduces: A temporal scale: dt ∈ ℝ_{>0} with units [s].

SE4.text: Single branch: all morphisms share the same spatial step length. Equivalent to SE2 in the isotropic case. In the multi-branch context it additionally forbids morphisms with step length k·a for k ≠ 1.
SE4.what_it_introduces: Absence of multiple coexisting step scales.

task2.conclusion: After imposing SE1–SE4, two free parameters remain: (a, dt). Rescaling (a, dt) → (k_a·a, k_t·dt) satisfies all four conditions for any k_a, k_t > 0, and gives c → (k_a/k_t)·c. Over the tested 25-point grid, 9 distinct c values appear, ranging from 5.0e-01 to 5.0e+07 m/s.
task2.c_invariant_under: simultaneous rescaling k_a = k_t (ratio a/dt preserved)
task2.c_not_invariant_under: independent rescaling of a and dt

abstract_cca_shared.epsilon: 1.0 per hom-set (single morphism per directed pair)
abstract_cca_shared.dagger: each morphism paired with its reverse
abstract_cca_shared.note: This abstract CCA is identical for all four models below

task3.verdict: COUNTEREXAMPLE CONFIRMED. Four models share the same abstract CCA structure. All satisfy SE1–SE4. They have four distinct propagation speeds: [8435.0, 9355.0, 5000.0, 10000.0] m/s. SE1–SE4 are therefore NOT sufficient to uniquely determine c.
task3.physical_note: Models M_A and M_B use silicon LA speeds at [100] and [111] orientations respectively. They correspond exactly to the experimental speed range 8435–9355 m/s cited in MICROSCOPIC_C2_COUPLING_DERIVATION_AUDIT.md. Both are physically plausible values for c in the C2 theory — and SE1–SE4 cannot distinguish between them.

SE5a_fix_a.statement: Fix the numerical value of a by identifying it with a known physical length.
examples: a = λ_phonon ≈ 1e-9 m (dominant phonon wavelength, empirical)
SE5a_fix_a.reason: Fixing a alone still leaves dt free; c = a/dt is undetermined without dt.

SE5b_fix_dt.statement: Fix the numerical value of dt by identifying it with a known physical time.
SE5b_fix_dt.reason: Fixing dt alone still leaves a free; c = a/dt is undetermined without a.

SE5c_fix_ratio.statement: Fix the ratio c = a/dt directly, either by derivation or measurement.
examples: c = ξ_c / (2τ_B) — empirical P3 ratio measurement
SE5c_fix_ratio.reason: If c is fixed, then a = c·dt and dt is still free, but c itself is determined. This is the only form that directly yields a unique numerical speed.
SE5c_fix_ratio.note: SE5c is the Gap 7 question itself: deriving c from the theory is equivalent to providing SE5c from an axiomatic route. GAP7_REDERIVATION.md showed 25 routes to derive SE5c all fail. This is now understood as: none of them provide a derivation of the ratio a/dt from within Ax1–Ax5.

SE5d_fix_both.statement: Fix both a and dt independently via two separate physical identifications.
SE5d_fix_both.example: a = λ_phonon AND dt = 1/omega_qubit → c = lambda_phonon * omega_qubit
SE5d_fix_both.reason: If both are fixed, c = a/dt is determined. Over-determines the system.
SE5d_fix_both.note: The two identifications must be independently motivated to avoid circularity.

task4.minimum_missing_condition: SE5c: fix the ratio c = a/dt
task4.nature_of_SE5: Always empirical or an additional axiomatic identification

rescaling_proof.conclusion: Rescaling is NOT forbidden by SE1–SE4. Simultaneous rescaling (k_a = k_t) preserves c. Independent rescaling (k_a ≠ k_t) changes c while satisfying all four conditions. Therefore SE1–SE4 are not sufficient to fix the numerical value of c.

task4.corrected_theorem_CUT: SE1–SE4 are necessary and sufficient for uniqueness of c UP TO THE FREEDOM c → (k_a/k_t)·c. A fifth condition SE5 is required to eliminate this freedom. The minimum SE5 is: fix c = a/dt directly (either by derivation or calibration). SE5 is always an empirical or external-physics input.

candidate_A.name: P3 ratio c_eff = ξ_c / (2τ_B)
candidate_A.reason: ξ_c = c / λ contains c. Measuring ξ_c from spatial correlation data is model-dependent: it requires fitting C_Γ(r) = K₀(r/ξ_c), which assumes the K₀ functional form. The ratio c_eff = ξ_c / (2τ_B) would correctly extract c IF ξ_c is independently measured AND the K₀ form is verified. Both require additional assumptions.
candidate_A.theory_prediction: c_eff = c (a free parameter needing SE5)
candidate_A.is_discriminating: Only if c_eff is orientation-independent AND TLS bath is excluded
candidate_A.data_available: Multi-qubit spatial correlation data (IBM devices): YES (in 06_datasets/)
candidate_A.limitation: TLS bath dominates and is isotropic — confounds orientation test

candidate_B.name: Orientation dependence of c_eff across crystal cuts
candidate_B.theory_prediction: D2 + SE2 (isotropic CCA): c_eff constant across orientations (value = c, free parameter)
candidate_B.null_prediction_phonon: Conventional LA phonon bath: c_eff varies by ~10.3% across orientations. Range: 8433.0–9134.2 m/s.
candidate_B.null_prediction_TLS: TLS bath: c_eff constant across orientations (same as D2)
candidate_B.is_discriminating: YES, if TLS bath is independently excluded. NO, if TLS dominates (both D2 and TLS predict orientation-independence).
candidate_B.data_available: NOT from existing IBM datasets — requires dedicated orientation experiment
candidate_B.required_precision: Need ξ_c measured to <4% across orientations (3σ on 11% variation)

from_existing_IBM_data.xi_c_measurement: Possible in principle from spatial qubit correlations
from_existing_IBM_data.tau_B_measurement: Extractable from non-Markovian onset in Ramsey curves
from_existing_IBM_data.c_eff_from_P3: Possible in principle — but requires K₀ functional form assumption
from_existing_IBM_data.orientation_test: NOT possible — requires chips with different crystal cuts
from_existing_IBM_data.TLS_exclusion: NOT possible from Ramsey data alone — requires echo spectroscopy

currently_testable.conclusion: From existing open data (IBM multi-qubit devices), one can estimate c_eff via the P3 ratio. This gives an empirical value for c (SE5d: empirical calibration). It does NOT test whether c is predicted by the theory. The orientation experiment would test whether c is orientation-independent (D2 prediction) vs. orientation-dependent (conventional phonon bath prediction), but requires data not currently available.

task5.verdict: No quantity in the theory is testable as a zero-free-parameter prediction. c is always a calibrated empirical input (SE5). The theory currently makes one conditional prediction: IF c is calibrated from one experiment (e.g., P3 on one chip orientation), THEN the same c should be recovered from other orientations IF D2+SE2 holds. This is the correct framing of the orientation experiment: a test of SELF-CONSISTENCY of the calibrated c, not a test of a derived c. It is discriminating against conventional LA phonon bath, but not against TLS bath.
task5.next_actionable_step: Measure c_eff from existing IBM spatial correlation data (P3 ratio) without assuming any orientation. This gives the empirical SE5 value. Then assess whether existing literature on qubit decoherence and spatial correlations provides an independent constraint on c_eff's orientation dependence.

overall_verdict.theorem_CUT_status: TOO STRONG as stated. SE1–SE4 are necessary and sufficient only for uniqueness of c up to independent rescalings of a and dt. A fifth condition SE5 is required for uniqueness of the numerical value of c.
overall_verdict.SE5_nature: Always empirical — a constitutive identification, not a derivation.
overall_verdict.gap7_restatement: GAP-7 is equivalent to: find SE5 from within the theory. All 25 routes in GAP7_REDERIVATION.md failed because they lacked SE5, not because they lacked SE1–SE4 (which are also assumptions, but at least structurally meaningful). The theory needs either a derivation of the physical scale of the CCA lattice, or must accept c as empirical.
